target.title: fix(ai): cache and case-insensitively match Azure deployment map
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`resolveAzureDeploymentNameFromMap` (in `packages/ai`) maps a model id to an Azure
deployment name on hot paths — it runs while building Azure Responses params for
every stream and lifecycle hook (`src/agents/openai-transport-stream.ts`,
`packages/ai/src/providers/azure-openai-responses.ts`). It had two problems:

1. **404s from case mismatches.** The lookup was case-sensitive. If
   `AZURE_OPENAI_DEPLOYMENT_NAME_MAP` maps `gpt-4o=deployment-gpt-4o` but the model
   id arrives as `GPT-4o`, the lookup missed and fell back to the **raw model id**;
   Azure then returned `404` "deployment not found".
2. **Re-parsing on every call.** It rebuilt a `Map` from the deployment-map string
   on every resolution, allocating and GC-ing on a hot path.

## Root Cause

```ts
return parseAzureDeploymentNameMap(params.deploymentMap).get(params.modelId) || params.modelId;
```

Parses the string every call, and `get(params.modelId)` is exact-case.

## What Changed

- Cache the parsed lookups per raw deployment-map string, bounded to 32 entries so
  memory stays flat even if a caller ever varies the input. **The cache is an
  in-memory, process-local `Map` (not persisted)** — no on-disk schema, no migration,
  and it is rebuilt from the env var on every process start.
- Resolve with **exact-case first, case-insensitive only as a fallback**. An exact
  key match always wins, so a config that intentionally distinguishes keys by case
  (`GPT-4o=prod-a,gpt-4o=prod-b`) keeps its exact mappings; the lowercased index only
  rescues ids that would otherwise 404 (`GPT-4o` against a `gpt-4o=...` map).
- Deployment names (the values) stay **verbatim** because Azure requires the exact
  deployment name; the fallback still returns the original-cased model id.

Both call sites are unchanged.

## Evidence

### Real behavior proof — provider path

Drives the real `streamSimpleAzureOpenAIResponses` provider path against a loopback
server (via the AI transport host fetch) and captures the **outgoing HTTP request
`model` field** — the deployment name Azure actually routes on:

```
Driving the real streamSimpleAzureOpenAIResponses provider path; capturing the outbound HTTP request on a loopback server.

PASS  mixed-case request resolves to the mapped deployment (was Azure 404 before the fix)
      AZURE_OPENAI_DEPLOYMENT_NAME_MAP="gpt-4o=deployment-gpt-4o"
      request model.id="GPT-4o"  ->  outgoing request body.model="deployment-gpt-4o"  (expected "deployment-gpt-4o")
PASS  exact-case mapping is preserved on the wire (no regression)
      AZURE_OPENAI_DEPLOYMENT_NAME_MAP="GPT-4o=prod-a,gpt-4o=prod-b"
      request model.id="GPT-4o"  ->  outgoing request body.model="prod-a"  (expected "prod-a")
PASS  unmapped model id falls back to the raw id on the wire
      AZURE_OPENAI_DEPLOYMENT_NAME_MAP="gpt-4o=deployment-gpt-4o"
      request model.id="gpt-5"  ->  outgoing request body.model="gpt-5"  (expected "gpt-5")

ALL PROVIDER-PATH CHECKS PASSED
```

This is codified as a committed integration test
(`packages/ai/src/providers/azure-openai-responses.deployment-map.test.ts`) so the
provider path stays covered in CI.

### Focused tests

`packages/ai/src/providers/azure-deployment-map.test.ts` (7) plus the provider-path
test (2) — 9 passed:

```
 ✓ preserves equals signs inside deployment names
 ✓ falls back to the model id when the map has no usable entry
 ✓ matches model ids case-insensitively when the request casing differs
 ✓ preserves the deployment name casing verbatim
 ✓ preserves the original model id casing on fallback
 ✓ prefers an exact-case match over the case-insensitive fallback
 ✓ caches the parsed lookup per deployment-map string
 ✓ sends the case-insensitively resolved deployment name on the wire
 ✓ keeps the exact-case deployment mapping on the wire (no regression)
```

### Performance

Standalone harness, 500,000 resolutions of the same map string:

```
  OLD (re-parses every call): 111.7 ms
  NEW (cached parse):         20.0 ms
  speedup: 5.6x fewer allocations on the hot path
```

AI-assisted.

Fixes #102936
